content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/get-payment-methods-filipino-digital-creators-working-today|COREMERCH guide to payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is building on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-webhook-driven-crypto-payment-fulfillment-explained-digital-3|cloudflare]] Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-explained-digital-4|Google Apps]] Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Presets stripe

When it comes to selling presets, Stripe is just one of many payment processors that can be used, but it's not the only option. Stripe operates in 46 countries out of 195 on earth, but that means 149 countries are left out. To fill this gap, alternative payment processors like PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy have emerged. However, each of these options comes with its own set of limitations, such as account suspension and transaction fees. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH provides a permanent structural alternative at the base layer, allowing creators to sell presets without relying on any single payment processor. This means that creators can continue to sell presets even if Stripe is not available in their country or if their PayPal account is suspended.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Restricted countries are a major issue for creators who want to sell presets using Stripe or other popular payment processors. Stripe operates in 46 countries, but that leaves a significant gap in coverage, particularly for creators in countries like Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan. PayPal, which is available in more countries than Stripe, still has its own set of limitations, including the risk of account suspension, which can hold funds for up to 180 days with no appeal. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH is not bound by the same geographical restrictions and can be used by creators in any country, regardless of the payment processor's availability. This means that creators can continue to sell presets without worrying about their country's restrictions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, each option has its own set of trade-offs. Stripe, for example, charges a flat fee of 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction, but it also has a reputation for being slow to process payments, which can lead to delayed payouts. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH uses a payment processor like NOWPayments, which has a lower fee of 0.5% and faster payment processing times. This means that creators can get paid faster and with less hassle. Additionally, COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) includes features like SPF/DKIM/DMARC configured and end-to-end testing, which can help reduce the risk of payment delays and lost sales.
COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) provides faster payment processing and lower fees than traditional payment processors like Stripe and PayPal.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

When it comes to ownership, automation, and delivery, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH provides a level of control and flexibility that's hard to find with traditional payment processors. With COREMERCH, creators can choose their own payment processor, automate their delivery and payment processes, and even configure their own SPF/DKIM/DMARC settings. This means that creators have full ownership and control over their sales and delivery processes, which can help reduce the risk of lost sales and revenue. In contrast, traditional payment processors like Stripe and PayPal often have strict rules and limitations that can limit a creator's ability to customize their sales and delivery processes.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

When it comes to choosing an architecture for selling presets, there are a few key considerations to keep in mind. First, consider the payment processor's availability in your country. If Stripe is not available, then a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH may be a better choice. Next, consider the payment processor's fees and payment processing times. If you want faster payment processing and lower fees, then COREMERCH's Edge Commerce Stack ($197) may be a better choice. Finally, consider the level of ownership and control you want over your sales and delivery processes. If you want full ownership and control, then a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH may be a better choice.
How do I sell digital products if Stripe is not available in my country?

The direct answer is NOWPayments combined with a sovereign commerce stack. NOWPayments is a crypto payment processor that requires no KYC from merchants and no account creation from buyers. It supports over 300 coins, charges 0.5% per transaction, and sends a webhook to your backend the moment payment confirms on-chain. Your backend — a Cloudflare Worker in Stack 02, a Google Apps Script Web App in Stack 01 — receives the webhook, verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email automatically. There is no platform that can suspend your access, no compliance team that can flag your account, no payout schedule that delays your revenue, and no company that can change the rules on you tomorrow.
A sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH gives creators full ownership and control over their sales and delivery processes.

You can also shop for COREMERCH's products at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Accept that no workaround inside conventional payment infrastructure is durable — platforms actively close gaps as they discover them. Create a NOWPayments account and configure wallet addresses for USDT on Tron and Bitcoin as your starting point — these cover the widest range of buyers in restricted markets. Choose your stack: Stack 01 for a self-deployed free setup using GitHub Pages and Google Apps Script, Stack 02 for the Edge Stack deployed by COREMERCH in 48 hours. Configure the NOWPayments webhook endpoint URL in your IPN settings pointing to your backend. Upload your product files to Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Complete a real mainnet test transaction and confirm the full pipeline: webhook received, transaction verified on-chain, order logged, delivery email sent, download link working. Share your store URL only after the mainnet test passes cleanly.
